title: U.S. House · North Carolina's 11th District
area: Western North Carolina, including Asheville and Buncombe County and all or part of Avery, Cherokee, Clay, Graham, Haywood, Henderson, Jackson, Macon, Madison, McDowell, Mitchell, Polk, Rutherford, Swain, Transylvania, and Yancey counties.

context.text: Incumbent Chuck Edwards won the March 3, 2026 Republican primary, but ended his re-election campaign on August 5, 2026, after the House Ethics Committee released a report finding he had "engaged in persistent unprofessional and inappropriate conduct" toward two female staffers and recommending he be censured. The North Carolina Republican Party selected North Carolina House member Jennifer Balkcom to replace Edwards as the Republican nominee on the November ballot. Jamie Ager won a five-way Democratic primary.

The Ethics Committee's report, based on a 25-page investigation, described Edwards giving two young staffers "lavish" gifts including jewelry, designer purses, and a KitchenAid mixer, inviting them on "intimate dinners and vacations," and sending personal notes; it said both staffers eventually left his office. Edwards's attorneys responded that the findings did not establish sexual harassment under House rules and that he "sincerely regrets that his behavior created discomfort," while his campaign said he "looks forward to having his name cleared." The full House voted to censure Edwards after he left the race.
Edwards remains a sitting member of Congress representing the 11th District through the end of his term but is not on the November 3, 2026 general election ballot.

summary.text: Jamie Ager is the Democratic nominee for North Carolina's 11th Congressional District, a Buncombe County farmer and co-founder of Hickory Nut Gap, a meat producer.

background.text: Born in Fairview, North Carolina; earned a high school diploma from A.C. Reynolds High School and bachelor's degrees in environmental studies and history from Warren Wilson College.

Career experience includes working as a farmer and co-founder of Hickory Nut Gap, which he describes as a sustainable meat producer; affiliated with the Buncombe County Farm Bureau and the Carolina Farm Stewardship Association.

priorities.text: Points to rising costs, Medicaid cuts, and increasingly severe weather as issues affecting his neighbors and his farm business.
priorities.quote: Rising costs hurt our businesses and our families. Medicaid insures my neighbors and my friends and now it's being ripped away. And the weather that batters us is only getting worse.

priorities.text: Frames his campaign as opposing policies he says favor wealthy interests over working Americans.
priorities.quote: Helping the rich get richer on the backs of hardworking Americans isn't working. In my humble opinion, it doesn't have to be this way.

positions.summary: Opposes cuts to Medicaid, saying it covers his neighbors and friends in the district.
positions.quote: Medicaid insures my neighbors and my friends and now it's being ripped away.

positions.summary: Points to worsening severe weather affecting western North Carolina, a region hit by Hurricane Helene, as a concern.
positions.quote: The weather that batters us is only getting worse.

candidates.name: Jennifer Balkcom
candidates.currentRole: Member, North Carolina House of Representatives, District 117 (since 2023)
candidates.ballotNote: Selected by the North Carolina Republican Party to replace Chuck Edwards on the general-election ballot after he ended his re-election campaign following an Ethics Committee censure recommendation. Balkcom had won her own re-election primary for her state House seat but will not appear on that ballot in November.

summary.text: Jennifer Balkcom is the Republican nominee for North Carolina's 11th Congressional District, a Henderson County mortgage loan officer and member of the North Carolina House of Representatives since 2023.

background.text: Born in Henderson County, North Carolina; earned a high school diploma from East Henderson High School and an associate degree from Blue Ridge Community College in 2016.

Career experience includes working as a small business owner and mortgage loan officer; has served as vice president of the Hendersonville Women's Club and the Hendersonville Lions Club, and as treasurer of the Mortgage Bankers Association of Western North Carolina.
Has served on the boards of the Henderson County Education Foundation, the AdventHealth Foundation Board, and the Henderson County Planning Board.

Elected to the North Carolina House of Representatives in 2022, representing District 117; assigned to the Agriculture, Banking, House Finance, Local Government (Land Use, Planning and Development), and State Government committees in the 2023-2024 session.

priorities.text: Points to sponsoring House Bill 805, the Prevent Sexual Exploitation of Women and Minors Act, and other criminal justice measures as a legislative priority.
priorities.quote: This session, Jennifer expanded her work on protecting women and children with House Bill 805, the Prevent Sexual Exploitation of Women and Minors Act, a major piece of legislation that strengthens protections against exploitation and abuse and is now state law.

priorities.text: Says protecting North Carolina farmland from foreign ownership and securing disaster relief for farmers are among her legislative priorities, drawing on growing up on a family farm in Henderson County.
priorities.quote: Jennifer's key initiatives in NC agriculture include legislation to provide disaster relief for farmers affected by natural disasters... and efforts to prevent discrimination in financing against agricultural producers. Additionally, she has introduced the NC Farmland and Military Protection Act to safeguard U.S. farmland from foreign ownership.

priorities.text: In a campaign ad, said she led an effort in the state legislature to prevent foreign ownership of North Carolina farmland.
priorities.quote: Protecting family farms is personal to me. That's why I led the effort in Raleigh to stop China and other enemies from owning or buying our farmland.

positions.summary: Sponsored state legislation strengthening penalties for violent offenders and felons caught with firearms.
positions.quote: She also advanced four additional criminal justice and public safety reforms that were signed into law. These measures strengthen penalties for violent offenders, ensure tougher sentencing for felons caught with firearms.

record.text: Sponsored North Carolina House Bill 805 (Prevent Sexual Exploitation of Women and Minors Act), which was signed into state law.
Sponsored the North Carolina Farmland and Military Protection Act, to restrict foreign ownership of North Carolina farmland.
Elected to the North Carolina House of Representatives in 2022, representing District 117; served on the Agriculture, Banking, House Finance, Local Government, and State Government committees.

summary.text: Travis Groo is the Libertarian Party candidate for North Carolina's 11th Congressional District.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of West Florida in 2000; works in transportation.

priorities.text: Lists balancing the federal budget, eliminating the federal income tax, and abolishing Certificate of Need laws as his three key campaign messages.
priorities.quote: Balance the budget. Get rid of the income tax. Abolish Certificate of Need (CON) laws.

priorities.text: Says property rights are the public policy area he is most passionate about.

positions.summary: Supports eliminating the federal income tax entirely rather than raising taxes on any income group.
positions.quote: Get rid of the income tax.
